grade.basis: Independent score-first opinion saved before opening prior reviews. Inspected all 28 score pages, including opening, pattern changes through V-AJ, chromatic closing pages and final bar. All parts retain treble clef, 2/4 and quarter=96; mostly continuous separately unmarked sixteenths, no double stops, chords, special bow strokes or extreme upper register. Violin 1 repeats its low one-octave ascending scale for much of the work, but violin 3 rises to A5 at V (m249, p16) with the recurring low E4-to-A5 jump, then descending G5-F5-E5-D5-C5. This introduces repeated string/position coordination beyond the first-violin scale; later flats change finger placement without increasing speed or register. Nine-minute sustained even semiquavers and repeated pattern changes require upper-intermediate control and stamina. Level 3 (ABRSM6/RCM7 advisory equivalent) is a best estimate within one level, without any automatic ensemble uplift.

findings.finding: Complete 28pp score inspected visually. Violin3 provides the hardest recurring register/leap pattern from V, rather than the largely scalar violin1. Technical estimate is based on individual notation, with duration counted as stamina rather than a four-player multiplier.
